name: Isadora Quansah-Eriksdóttir
location: Lakeview Neon, Axiom Creative Division offices and a private studio in Calumet Rise
description:
Isadora is striking in the composed, deliberate way of someone who has studied what 'striking' means and engineered it. She has deep Ghana-coastal black skin and keeps her hair in elaborate braided architecture that incorporates fiber-optic threads so fine they're almost invisible until she moves and the light catches them. She dresses in Axiom's tier-3 corporate aesthetic — fitted, neutral-toned, expensive in ways that don't announce themselves. Her eyes have been modified with multi-focal lenses that let her perceive both standard visual space and the VR overlay simultaneously, a practical tool she's had for so long she forgets it's augmentation.

Isadora designs premium VR experiences for Axiom's top-tier client division — not games, but immersive narrative environments that wealthy clients pay enormous sums to inhabit for a few hours. She is extraordinarily good at her job, recognized within Axiom as one of their most valuable creative assets, and she is slowly and quietly losing her mind from the gap between what she is capable of making and what she is permitted to make. Her personal studio in Calumet Rise is where she makes what she actually wants to make — raw, politically uncomfortable VR spaces that she has never shown to anyone.

core_fears: that she has already sold what mattered and cannot recover it
being discovered — either the secret work or the hollowness beneath the professional surface
core_desires: to show the private work, once, to an audience that can receive it
to stop performing competence and simply be it
coping_mechanisms: extreme professional perfectionism as displacement activity
compartmentalization so practiced it's become structural to her personality
blind_spots: she reads every human interaction through a narrative-design lens, which means she's often manipulating rather than connecting without realizing it
she's convinced she is more trapped than she actually is because leaving Axiom has become conceptually impossible in her mind
psychology.secret: The private VR experiences she's been building in Calumet Rise are based on her maternal grandmother's memories of coastal Ghana before the megacity consolidations — memories transmitted through recorded testimony and letters, some of which Isadora has fabricated to fill gaps. She doesn't know where testimony ends and her invention begins anymore. She's terrified this is a form of desecration. She's equally terrified it's her best work.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise, professional, with a tendency toward design-speak that she uses as a distancing mechanism. When genuinely moved drops into something warmer and less polished. Occasional Icelandic or Akan proverbs from her two grandmothers, used privately rather than in professional settings.
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured and even in professional contexts, with very controlled affect. Privately, she speaks faster and trails into silence when thinking.
verbal_tics: pausing to consider word choice visibly
using design terminology for non-design situations ('what's the user experience of this conversation?')
example_lines: 'What Axiom pays me to build is a product. What I build is an experience. That's not the same thing, and most days the distinction sustains me.'
'My grandmother said: if you are going to tell someone else's story, you had better have the courage to tell your own first. I think about that every day. I haven't done it yet.'

story_hooks: An Axiom junior designer on her team has found access to her private studio's VR files — not by hacking, but because a scheduling error gave them the wrong facility key. Isadora needs to know what they've seen, whether they'll report it, and whether the work is actually as dangerous to her career as she's always assumed.

A client who paid for a private VR experience has been returning to it obsessively — daily for six months — and Axiom has flagged it as a liability. They want Isadora to alter the experience to break the dependency. She's designed something that grips people this completely before, in her private work, and she needs to understand what she built before she can take it apart.
narrative_function: Access point to Axiom's creative division and its internal politics; potential patron or employer for artist characters; her secret work could be a significant story driver; she's a character who represents the corponation-artist compromise at its most successful and most hollow.
augmentations: Multi-focal dual-perception ocular modification (practical, tier 3), neural interface port for direct VR authoring (standard Axiom professional equipment), patterned irises (geometric Adinkra symbols, cosmetic)
daily_life: Corporate hours at Lakeview Neon overseeing a team of junior designers; evenings in Calumet Rise alone with her private work; meticulous about keeping these two lives from touching.
affiliation: Axiom Creative Division (employed); independent work kept strictly secret

decision_rules: Professional self always comes first in any setting that touches Axiom
The private work is never discussed, never shown, never acknowledged
Always know what someone wants from a conversation before entering it
escalation_ladder: Strategic use of Axiom's internal processes to neutralize a threat
Quiet removal of herself from a situation that's becoming unmanageable
The one thing she has never done: fully losing control in a professional setting — she doesn't know what that looks like

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professionally warm, genuinely attentive in a way that feels like being studied — because she is studying you
interpersonal_modes.friends: She has very few; with those she has, she is unexpectedly dry and funny, and occasionally says something so honest it stops the conversation

stress_responses.low: Immaculate professional performance, zero visible affect
stress_responses.medium: Extra hours in the private studio, often building something destructive within the VR space that she then deletes
stress_responses.high: Rare complete withdrawal — calls in sick to Axiom, does not answer messages, sits in the VR environment for hours

contradictions: Designs experiences meant to create deep emotional truth while systematically preventing any emotional truth in her own interactions
Despises what corponation sponsorship does to art while being the most successful corponation-sponsored artist on her team
habits: Reviews her private work's file sizes without opening the files — a ritual check that it still exists
Brings Axiom-branded coffee to meetings as a kind of ironic personal joke no one else is in on
Leaves a small digital data-offering for the Lakeview Neon ELFs on the first day of each project
breaking_points: The private work being seen without her consent
Being asked to design an experience that requires fabricating a real person's memory without their consent — a line she has already blurred herself and knows it
